blocks.help: Leaves the innermost loop.
Skips the rest of this round of the innermost loop.
Counts from one number to another, running blocks for each value.
Repeats blocks forever (use stop or break to leave).
Runs blocks only when a condition is true. Add else if and else parts with ⊕, and remove them with ⊖.
Repeats blocks a number of times.
Repeats blocks while a condition is true; choose until in the menu to repeat until it becomes true.
The message of an error that a catch part caught.
Throws the error this catch part caught again, for a try block further out to catch. It can only be used inside a catch part.
Stops the blocks here with an error of this kind and this message. The nearest try block around it that catches the kind runs its catch part next; with none, the program stops.

Runs the blocks after try. If one of them throws an error, the first catch part for that kind of error runs, with the error in its variable; the parts are tried in order, and std::exception catches every kind. Add catch parts with ⊕ and remove them with ⊖.
Calls a function and uses its result.
Calls a function.
Defines a function: a named group of blocks you can use again.
Leaves the function, giving back a value if the function returns one.
Asks the user to type something and stores it in a variable.
From here on, prints every decimal number with this many digits after the decimal point, also in join and as text. Whole numbers are not changed.
Shows values in the console.
True or false.
True when the condition is false.
True when all (and) or any (or) of the conditions are true.
One of two values, depending on a condition.
The number without its minus sign.
Adds, subtracts, multiplies or divides two numbers, or gives the remainder.
The number if it is between the two limits, otherwise the nearer limit. The lower limit must not be above the higher one: a debug build stops the program then.
Compares two values.
Converts a number to another number type, e.g. a decimal to a whole number.
A function of a number: rounding, roots, powers of e, logarithms, and the angle functions, whose angles are in radians. The result is a decimal number.

A function of two numbers: the first to the power of the second; the angle, in radians, of the point whose y is the first and whose x is the second; or the long side of a right-angled triangle whose other sides are the two.
The larger or the smaller of two numbers.
A number, such as 42 or 3.14.
A random whole number between the two values, including both.
A random decimal number between the two values.
Ends the program. Exit code 0 means success.
The program starts here. A project has exactly one of these blocks.

A value as text, written as print writes it: a decimal number with the decimal places 'show numbers with' chose, true or false for a true/false value. A struct cannot be turned into text in one go; join its fields instead.
The text in lowercase or in uppercase. Only the letters A to Z change; every other character stays as it is.
A single character, such as 'a'.
Whether a text contains another text, starts with it or ends with it.
Joins text and numbers into one piece of text.
The number of characters in a text.
The character at a position of a text, counting from 0. A position outside the text stops the program with an out-of-range error.
A piece of text.
The characters of a text from a position, counting from 0, up to this many of them; fewer when the text ends first. A start past the end of the text stops the program with an out-of-range error.
The text with every place where the first text occurs replaced by the second. An empty first text changes nothing.
A list of the parts of a text between its separators. Two separators in a row give an empty part, and an empty separator gives one part for each character.

The number at the start of a text: 12abc gives 12. A text that does not start with a number throws an invalid argument error, and a number too large for its type throws an out-of-range error; the Errors category has the blocks that catch them.
The text without the spaces and tabs at its start and end.
Adds to a variable (+=); choose down by (-=), times (*=), divided by (/=) or mod (%=) in the menu to subtract, multiply, divide or keep the remainder instead.
Creates a variable. It can be used by the blocks after it in the same place.
The value of a variable.
Gives a variable a new value.
